1946, February 28
Mrs. E'd Helena Wilhite
Page 2
May 29th. "Mrs Nagle as above May 25th. Thanks be to God: fear - ful pains and swelling gone from abdomen, has good appetite and eating fine. Husband enrolls Poor Souls again in thanksgiving."
Sept. 14th, Brooklyn, N. Y. "Mrs. Nagle as noted above May 25 and 29th, here Today in perfect health. =
I hardly know what to do to keep the letters here from piling up. Otherwise I'd give you a number of the cases that we've had here at St. Michael's lately. I feel I must give you the second last note of the very few I have time and call to record.
Feb. 15, 1946. " ... Catherine Mahon of Woodside, L. I. enrolled August 25th, 1945, having lost nearly half of her brain by operation on "brain-tumor" - doctors absolutely hopeless of her recovery. Two days later an enrollment was sent for the Poor Souls. From that day she be- gan to come back to herself. For several weeks was unable to remember - even faces - consequently could not recognize anyone. ... Now, thanks be to God, the brains seem to have grown back in place. She is figur- ing on coming to St. Michael's as soon as the weather permits. Again Deo Gratias.
But why worry? "To worry about anything" St. Therese, the Little Flower claims, "is to indicate a want of confidence in God." She very likely speaks of excessive worrying; and yet, why should we worry a- bout anything - tumors? Cancers? Death? Why not rather turn to God, Whose solicitude for our individual welfare - temporarily as well as spiritually - puts all created solicitude out of the picture. Why not foster confidence in His divine Providence by humbly and in all child- like humility venture to remind Him - remind Him in the Person of our divine Brother Jesus - that we are His children - that we are, and at least want to be reckoned as amongst Eis "little ones"; and therefore, thank Him frequently for, not only the blessings of the past and pre- sent, but thank Him ahead of time for whatever He foresees is pleasing to Him that we suffer, and this not only in general but in each parti- cular case - leaving everything absolutely in His divine disposal, in- cluding with all its circumstances, when, where, and how He may be pleased to dispose the event of our death.
